c24.title: C24

war_stories.title: Side Cap Thermal Warping
war_stories.crisis: Application of rubberized soft paint and subsequent oven curing caused the ABS side caps to twist and bow, resulting in parts that did not fit the chassis geometry.
war_stories.fix: Rejected the vendor's flat-rack curing method and engineered a 'Vertical Hanging Fixture' to utilize gravity to maintain straightness during the bake cycle.
war_stories.metric: Flatness deviation reduced from >2.50mm to acceptable limits

war_stories.title: Headphone Jack Serviceability Redesign
war_stories.crisis: The original design required removing the entire front bolster and 5-6 faders to replace the headphone jack, which was a high-frequency failure item.
war_stories.fix: Redesigned the sheet metal bracket and plastic bolster to recess the jack, allowing it to be serviced by removing only the bottom pan and a single nut.
war_stories.metric: 4.8% field failure rate (based on legacy data)

war_stories.title: Top Panel Fabrication Blockage
war_stories.crisis: The primary overseas vendor issued a 'no-bid' on the top panel due to the high density of welded standoffs and hole features, threatening the Pilot build schedule.
war_stories.fix: Implemented a dual-sourcing strategy using Mass Precision for rapid prototypes and negotiated a manual offset-welding process with the overseas vendor to bridge the gap.

war_stories.title: Jog Wheel Integration
war_stories.crisis: The mandate to lower costs required replacing the legacy custom encoder with a smaller commodity part (Bourns EM14), creating a mismatch with the industrial design feel.
war_stories.fix: Engineered a custom plastic surround and LED holder to adapt the 14mm encoder to the larger chassis opening, maintaining the premium 'scrub' feel.

war_stories.title: PCB Interference & DCD Protocol
war_stories.crisis: High component density led to physical interferences, such as power connectors on the SubMix I/O board clashing with the chassis.
war_stories.fix: Enforced a strict Data Control Drawing (DCD) protocol, requiring PCB designers to route within mechanical keep-outs, forcing connector relocations.

war_stories.title: Cosmetic CMF Defense
war_stories.crisis: Early units exhibited 'Dental White' (yellowish) silkscreening and visible metal ripples/dents along bend lines that warped the graphics.
war_stories.fix: Rejected inferior samples and enforced strict adherence to 'Spectral Master' color standards and Class A surface inspection criteria.

bio_bullets: • Situation: The C|24 console required integrating 19 distinct Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) into a low-profile chassis with zero margin for interference. Task: Establish a governance protocol to ensure mechanical and electrical design synchronization and prevent costly board spins. Action: Architected and enforced a strict Data Control Drawing (DCD) system, authoring binding geometric constraints for every PCB. I managed up to 13 revisions per board (e.g., MicPre 8 I/O), personally resolving connector collisions and keep-out violations before layout finalization. Result: Achieved 100% mechanical fit on the first physical build, eliminating interference issues for the entire product line.

• Situation: During the critical Pilot phase, the "Side Cap" cosmetic parts failed inspection due to severe thermal warping caused by the vendor's standard paint curing process. Task: Diagnose the root cause and engineer a manufacturing solution to save the yield without slipping the schedule. Action: I engaged in technical diplomacy with the vendor (Jetcrown), rejecting their flat-rack process. I engineered a specific "Vertical Hanging Fixture" workflow that utilized gravity to straighten parts during the cure cycle and formalized this process via ECO 12740 (Rev C to D). Result: Eliminated the warp defect, ensuring parts met the "Spectral Master DS-022" aesthetic standard and protecting the Mass Production launch timeline.

• Situation: The primary overseas contract manufacturer (VTech/Kwanta) issued a "no-bid" on the product's main top panel due to the high density of welded hardware, threatening the Pilot build. Task: Secure parts for the immediate build while establishing a viable long-term production capability. Action: I orchestrated a dual-sourcing strategy, leveraging domestic partner Mass Precision for rapid-turn Pilot units while simultaneously negotiating with overseas engineers to validate a manual offset-welding process to bridge the gap until automation came online. Result: Delivered Pilot units on schedule and successfully qualified the long-term overseas manufacturing process for the product's most complex component.

• Situation: The engineering team faced data integrity risks during a complex transition to RoHS compliance and a Product Data Management (PDM) system upgrade. Task: Establish departmental data governance to prevent file corruption and ensure version control across the team. Action: I administered the Pro/Intralink 8.0 server migration and authored the "General Modeling Guide" for the department. I organized and led mandatory "User Orientation" training sessions, enforcing strict check-in/check-out protocols. Result: Maintained 100% data integrity for thousands of production files and preserved complex assembly relationships during the critical RoHS Bill of Materials conversion.

• Situation: The transition from Prototype to Mass Production involved a complex Bill of Materials (BOM) with over 30 custom molds and 15 sheet metal parts. Task: Execute rigorous Configuration Management to ensure all global vendors were building to the correct revision. Action: I acted as the primary Originator for all mechanical releases, authoring comprehensive Engineering Change Orders (e.g., ECO 12263 for Metal, ECO 12262 for Plastics). I defined precise material dispositions (Scrap vs. Use-As-Is) to minimize scrap costs while strictly enforcing new revision standards. Result: Successfully released the entire mechanical product structure to production, synchronizing a global supply chain across the US and China with zero revision-mismatch errors.
